taste.where: side_l and front34: the front fender, nose corners and bumper are one plain black field about a door in size. Its own tone blocks don't show, and it only gets the curved strakes, while the door and haunch carry three block sizes and tones.

front34, crop-nose and top: the bonnet has a thin band of dark brown blocks and a few terracotta slivers at its edges. The bumper, splitter area and nose corners are bare black. The rear deck and engine cover in rear34 and top are dense, layered collage.

fixes.text: The front is plainer than the tail. In front34 and crop-nose the bumper, nose corners and front fender sides are bare black. The black field's darker tone blocks don't show at 10 m, and the bonnet has only one thin band of brown blocks. Side_l's front fender is a plain black panel up to a hard stepped edge. The rear deck and haunch, by contrast, carry big, medium and dust-sized blocks in several tones. The nose needs the collage as layered as the tail has it.

There is too little close-up detail for a raced car. Side_l shows no roster sponsors on the flank at all, only two marks on the rear bumper. Side_r has only HUILEC and two small marks on the sill. The sill pinline the brief describes isn't visible in either side shot. The paper field's own tone blocks are so close to the paper that the haunch reads flat at 10 m in side_l and crop-beltline. The favourites (24, 21) carry dozens of small marks on sills, bumpers and mirrors.

The curved, tapering terracotta strokes on the front fender vents and the bumper corners (front34, crop-nose) read as flame licks or claw marks, a second visual language next to the square pixel blocks. The brief drops flame tongues.

lint_missed: In side_r's lighting the paper reads mid-grey and the terracotta reads brown, so the right side loses the light tail and goes muddy at distance (side_r-distance). The left side doesn't have this problem.
The rear number's dark brown block wraps round the rear corner, so from side_r a clipped '45' shows at the tail.
In side_r the 451 door block sits beside other dark brown blocks of the same tone and merges with them, so the number panel's edge is lost. In side_l it stands clear.

answers.note: The black's tone is now #403E3C (the theme's uiAlt; #282726 vanished on #100F0F), and the black carries its own collage that grows towards the nose: big, 40 px and 16 px blocks of #403E3C, #6B3528 and terracotta embers (nose_density 0.5 over nose_reach 0.3), plus 40 px tone blocks anywhere in the black. The bumper corners under the headlights get scattered 40/20 px blocks on their own islands, because the side views map them only in slivers. Sim 20261021-223305: front34 shows the bonnet, the fender tops and the corners under the headlights layered in three sizes and three tones. top shows the bonnet as dense as the engine cover. side_l shows grey and brown blocks on the front fender ahead of the arch. The grille, crash opening and lower bumper face stay black and carbon: their islands are too small or too dark for blocks that show (24 px blocks on the splitter top measured 3.5 px on screen).

Sim 20261021-223305. side_l now carries flank marks where its low camera sees them (the verge hides the sill there): Altmere and Norvane marks in paper ahead of the number, on one centre line with the extinguisher E above them and 64 px clear of the number, and a black HEXMOOR wordmark on the paper above the rear arch. side_r and rear34 show the same marks. The paper's dark tone blocks are now #878580 next to #B7B5AC and #F2F0E5, so the haunch reads as blocks at 10 m in side_l, side_r and rear34. The sill pinline is 20 px (was 14) and stops at the number block. It shows as a terracotta step line on top of the black sill under the paper in side_r. Over the terracotta core it is terracotta on terracotta, and in side_l the verge hides the sill. With the sill, tail, bonnet and deck marks, the car now carries 23 marks.

The intake strakes are #100F0F now, so no curved accent strokes are left at the nose. front34 in sim 20261021-223305 shows the bumper corners with square blocks only. The only terracotta at the nose is the splitter lip and the square embers.

fixes.text: The terracotta core is now the plainest part of the car. In side_l, side_r and front34 the door and the front of the rear haunch form one flat terracotta field, larger than a door. It runs from the black front fender back to the paper blocks and from the beltline to the sill, broken only by the 451 block, the E and two small marks. The roof's share of the same core is dense with dark brown, black and paper blocks in the top view, and the brief asks for the core to be the densest area. Paul Miller's door (anchor 24) carries blocks of its own tones right around the number. The side views need that too.

Close-up detail is better but still thin next to 21 and 24. The mirrors are bare terracotta. The nose and bumper carry no small marks in front34. Side_r's flank ahead of the number has only two small marks. The terracotta pinline along the top of the sill can't be seen in side_r or front34. Getspeed carries marks on its sills, bumpers, mirrors and wing.

blocked: The sim's rear number sits on the rear bumper corner and wraps round it, so side_r shows a clipped '45' on its dark brown block at the tail. The number reads whole in rear34.

answers.note: The core's own big blocks are now placed at core_fill 0.6 on the sides (was 0.25; the roof keeps 0.25 as top_core_fill, it was dense already), and among them are black blocks towards the front split and paper blocks towards the rear one (core_mix 0.4). Inside the core, mid and big blocks no longer draw plain terracotta, which didn't show on it. Sim 20261022-032434: in side_r the door and the front of the haunch carry big #6B3528 blocks above and behind the number, paper blocks reaching up from the sill, and black dust round the marks ahead of it. side_l and front34 show the same: dark brown, paper and grey blocks from the number back to the paper. What is left plain is the strip between the front arch and the number, which holds the flank marks and the number's keep-clear.

Sim 20261022-032434. Mirrors: a black Drexa star mark on each terracotta shell (side_l, side_r, front34), placed off the shell's fold. Flank: a third paper mark (Zentiq) under the Altmere/Norvane pair ahead of the number, so the column reads mark pair, bolt, with the E above (side_l, side_r, front34). Sill pinline: it is now paper where the terracotta core sits on the sill and terracotta under the black and paper, so it shows its whole length: in side_r it runs as a paper step line from the front arch to the number and as a terracotta line under the paper slab; in front34 the paper line shows under the core. Nose: AVELOR on the bonnet front reads whole in front34 and top. The Hexmoor and Zentiq marks either side of it were cut by the bonnet's curved seams, so they are gone. The bumper corners under the headlights take no marks: no view maps front_bumper_corner_l / _r (i021 / i020) except as slivers at side u 0-0.133, so a sponsor has no car-space anchor there (kit map, see notes). The car now carries 25 sponsor marks and four race markings.

The door number blocks have a 16 px paper (#DAD8CE) keyline round them, so they keep their edge whatever block sits beside them. In side_r of sim 20261022-032434 the 451 block is framed all round and stands clear of the dark brown blocks at its upper left. In side_l and front34 the frame shows too, joining the paper blocks where they meet it.

orders.where: The doors decide it. On side_l and side_r, A builds the number block into the collage. It has a paper keyline frame around the #6B3528 451 block, stepped dark and paper blocks around it, and layered terracotta tones from the front fender back to the haunch. In B the whole door ahead of the number and above the sill is one plain terracotta field, bigger than a door, and the number block has no keyline. That fails `boring` and goes against the brief's "no plain field". The same gap shows on front34, where B's door is a flat orange slab and A's carries the stepped frame and darker blocks. On top, B's right flank strip behind the mirror is also plainer. The nose, bonnet, roof and tail are close to identical in both. B's AVELOR is smaller and more discreet, but that doesn't outweigh the plain doors.

B is the better car, and the doors and the core decide it. Side_l and front34: in A, the door, the front of the haunch and the B-pillar are one plain terracotta field bigger than a door, with the 451 block sitting alone on it. That fails the boring check, and it is the "confetti on a plain car" layout the brief rules out. In B the same area is a stacked collage: #6B3528 and paper blocks in more than one size reach in from the roof and the haunch. Side_r has the same difference: A's door ahead of the light panel is mostly flat terracotta, while B layers darker terracotta and paper steps across it. In both sides' shots, B's 451 sits in its solid #6B3528 block inside a paper keyline, as the brief asks, and the frame still reads in the distance images. A's block has no keyline and its edges fade into the field. B also carries a second hazard mark ahead of the number, and its roof and windscreen-pillar collage is denser, seen from front34 and side_l. Top and rear34 are close to the same. B's bonnet AVELOR is larger and more tracked; it's still discreet and doesn't make the layout wordmark-led. In top, the tail (DREXA, BRANDVIK) is effectively the same. Neither car changes the nose, the bumper or the engine cover in a way that decides it.

fixes.title: Side change leans backwards, black is only a snout
fixes.detail: From the side, the black stops at the front arch. The terracotta then reaches furthest back low on the haunch, almost to the rear arch in side_r and through the big low blocks in side_l, while at the roof it ends over the B-pillar. So the change from black to paper leans against the car's motion instead of reading as the brief's one raked slash, and side-on the car reads as a terracotta-and-paper car with a black nose.
